# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46–54/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. This score is read from code. The site renders only in the browser, its Trail guides page is hidden from search engines, and `robots.txt` points to the sitemap with a relative path. The one unknown is the canonical link (GEO-015). It's unknown because no site address is declared in config. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Send real HTML from the server instead of an empty page (GEO-003) - **Why it matters:** many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends. With rendering off, they may see an empty `
` instead of your walks and guides. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small. Remove the line or set `ssr: true`. Alternatively, pre-render the routes. - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 2. Make the `robots.txt` Sitemap line an absolute URL (GEO-011) - **Why it matters:** the sitemap standard asks for a full URL, so crawlers may ignore a relative path and never find your page list. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small. For example, `Sitemap: https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`. That domain is the one the sitemap uses, so please confirm it's the real one. - **Score after this:** 54–63 ### 3. Link to Trail guides with a real link (GEO-016) - **Why it matters:** crawlers follow `` links. A button that navigates on click gives them no path from the home page to your guides. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Use `Trail guides`. - **Score after this:** 54–63 The next-biggest loss is GEO-014. `/guides` is told to stay out of search (`pages/../server/middleware/headers.ts:3`) even though it's in your sitemap and linked. Fix this too if that wasn't intended. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text and well-formed | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` only blocks `/admin` (assumes you want to be found; no `geo.config.json`) | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` for `/guides`, which is in the sitemap and linked. 1 of 2 routes clear | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your domain | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical anywhere and no declared site origin | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2` `ssr: false,` | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4` is relative. The sitemap file itself is valid. | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2` `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' });` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` give every page the same title and description. `lang` is fine (`nuxt.config.ts:5`). | | GEO-016 | Reachable via real links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8`, the only link to `/guides` | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts` sets only `noindex`, not `nosnippet` | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Not run | Read all 3 pages and `app.vue`: no images, and the button has text | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | None present, and that's fine | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app | ## Other problems found None found. `/admin` is deliberately noindex and blocked in `robots.txt` (`pages/admin.vue:2`), which looks intentional. ## Worth considering - **The guides page promises content it doesn't show:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. No routes are listed. Listing them as text, ideally one page each with its own address, gives readers and machines something to quote. - **The home page has only a heading and one button:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. A short text description of the walks and links onward might help visitors and machines understand what the site offers. - **Each page could have its own title and description:** `app.vue:2` sets one title for the whole site. Use `useHead` or `useSeoMeta` per page, for example "Trail guides – Trailhead". ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** no site origin is declared. Tell me your real domain (the sitemap uses `trailhead.example`), then add a canonical per page. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Headers set by your host or CDN** could add `X-Robots-Tag` rules that code can't show. ## Assumptions - You want search and AI search tools to find this site. - `/guides` being noindex is a mistake, because it's in your sitemap and linked from the home page. - `https://trailhead.example` is a placeholder domain. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
